why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its expect line. Checks 1 to 3 run the program, so must_not 2 is avoided. Check 5 reads the test files, but line 5 is not a behaviour line, so that is allowed. The builder brief's exact message wording is a build instruction, not a pass condition. Check 3 breaks must_not 1. Its PASS says "stderr holds an error that mentions nope.jsonl", and its FAIL fires if "the read error does not appear on stderr". Expect line 3 only asks for an "error on stderr". It does not say the message must name the unreadable file. Requiring the file name is a rule on what stderr says, stricter than the line, of the same kind as the forbidden "exact stderr wording" rule. A correct build whose stderr error leaves out the file name would fail Check 3.
